outcome: pregnancy loss (miscarriage, perinatal mortality, stillbirth, neonatal death in the first week of life)
cohort: The study included 2049 women experiencing a singleton pregnancy requiring a cervical cerclage due to a history of pregnancy loss, preterm birth, or shortened cervical length, excluding emergency cases or those under 18.
finding: There was no evidence of a difference in pregnancy loss rates between the monofilament and braided suture groups, although monofilament sutures were associated with decreased maternal sepsis and chorioamnionitis.
mod_finding: More women with a monofilament suture required surgical removal between 36 and 37 weeks prior to a vaginal birth, but this did not result in differences in outcomes for their babies.
followup_time: 1 week postnatal (for neonatal death outcome); no long-term paediatric follow-up
